3. 
4. //==================================================================================================
5. // Imports
6. //==================================================================================================
7. 
8. use vstd::prelude::*;
9. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
10. include!("table.spec.rs");
11. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
12. include!("table.proof.rs");
13. 
14. use super::{
15.     PteWord,
16.     PTE_WORD_SIZE_LOG2,
17. };
18. 
19. //==================================================================================================
20. // Table Entry Trait
21. //==================================================================================================
22. 
23. ///
24. /// # Description
25. ///
26. /// Trait bound for entry types that can be stored in a page table.
27. ///
28. /// The raw representation uses [`PteWord`] — `u32` on x86.
29. ///
30. #[verus_verify]
31. pub trait TableEntry: Copy {
32.     /// Creates from a raw [`PteWord`], returning `None` if the value is invalid.
33.     #[verus_spec(result =>
34.         ensures result == spec_entry_from_raw::<Self>(raw),
35.     )]
36.     fn from_raw(raw: PteWord) -> Option<Self>;
37.     /// Returns the raw [`PteWord`] representation.
38.     #[verus_spec(result =>
39.         ensures result == spec_entry_raw(self),
40.     )]
41.     fn raw(self) -> PteWord;
42. }
43. 
44. //==================================================================================================
45. // Table Index
46. //==================================================================================================
47. 
48. ///
49. /// # Description
50. ///
51. /// A validated index into a page table, guaranteed to be in `[0, PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH)`.
52. ///
53. #[verus_verify]
54. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
55. pub struct TableIndex(usize);
56. 
57. #[verus_verify]
58. impl TableIndex {
59.     ///
60.     /// # Description
61.     ///
62.     /// Creates a [`TableIndex`] from a raw `usize`, returning `None` if the value is out of
63.     /// bounds.
64.     ///
65.     #[verus_spec(result =>
66.         ensures
67.             match result {
68.                 Some(t) => index < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH && t@ == index as nat,
69.                 None => index >= crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
70.             },
71.     )]
72.     pub const fn new(index: usize) -> Option<Self> {
73.         if index < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH {
74.             Some(Self(index))
75.         } else {
76.             None
77.         }
78.     }
79. 
80.     ///
81.     /// # Description
82.     ///
83.     /// Returns the underlying index value.
84.     ///
85.     #[verus_spec(result =>
86.         ensures
87.             result as nat == self@,
88.             result < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
89.     )]
90.     pub const fn into_raw(self) -> usize {
91.         proof! { use_type_invariant(self); }
92.         self.0
93.     }
94. }
95. 
96. //==================================================================================================
97. // Virtual Address Index Extraction
98. //==================================================================================================
99. 
100. /// Extracts the PD index (bits 22-31) from a virtual address as a [`TableIndex`].
101. #[verus_spec(result =>
102.     ensures
103.         result@ == spec_pd_index(vaddr),
104.         result@ < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
105. )]
106. pub const fn pd_index(vaddr: usize) -> TableIndex {
107.     proof! { assert(crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH == 1024) by (compute); }
108.     // The mask guarantees the result is always < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH.
109.     let index: usize = (vaddr >> crate::mem::PGTAB_SHIFT) & (crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1);
110.     proof! {
111.         assert(crate::mem::PGTAB_SHIFT == 22) by (compute);
112.         assert(index < 1024) by (bit_vector)
113.             requires index == (vaddr >> 22usize) & 1023usize;
114.     }
115.     TableIndex(index)
116. }
117. 
118. /// Extracts the PT index (bits 12-21) from a virtual address as a [`TableIndex`].
119. #[verus_spec(result =>
120.     ensures
121.         result@ == spec_pt_index(vaddr),
122.         result@ < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
123. )]
124. pub const fn pt_index(vaddr: usize) -> TableIndex {
125.     proof! { assert(crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH == 1024) by (compute); }
126.     // The mask guarantees the result is always < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH.
127.     let index: usize = (vaddr >> crate::mem::PAGE_SHIFT) & (crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1);
128.     proof! {
129.         assert(crate::mem::PAGE_SHIFT == 12) by (compute);
130.         assert(index < 1024) by (bit_vector)
131.             requires index == (vaddr >> 12usize) & 1023usize;
132.     }
133.     TableIndex(index)
134. }
135. 
136. //==================================================================================================
137. // Table
138. //==================================================================================================
139. 
140. ///
141. /// # Description
142. ///
143. /// A page-table page containing [`PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`](crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH) entries.
144. ///
145. /// This type is parameterized over the entry type to enforce that each table level uses only
146. /// its own entry kind (e.g., PD tables only [`PageDirectoryEntry`], PT tables only
147. /// [`PageTableEntry`]).
148. ///
149. /// The table is accessed via a base address that must be valid in the current address space
150. /// (i.e., a mapped virtual address). It does not own the backing memory — the caller is
151. /// responsible for allocation and lifetime management.
152. ///
153. #[verus_verify]
154. #[derive(Debug)]
155. pub struct Table<E: TableEntry> {
156.     /// Base address of the table (must be page-aligned).
157.     base: usize,
158.     /// Phantom marker for the entry type.
159.     _marker: ::core::marker::PhantomData<E>,
160. }
161. 
162. #[verus_verify]
163. impl<E: TableEntry> Table<E> {
164.     ///
165.     /// # Description
166.     ///
167.     /// Creates a table reference from a base address.
168.     ///
169.     /// # Safety
170.     ///
171.     /// `base` must be a valid, page-aligned address with at least one page of readable/writable
172.     /// memory.
173.     ///
174.     #[verus_spec(result =>
175.         ensures result@.addr == base as nat,
176.     )]
177.     pub const unsafe fn from_address(base: usize) -> Self {
178.         Self {
179.             base,
180.             _marker: ::core::marker::PhantomData,
181.         }
182.     }
183. 
184.     ///
185.     /// # Description
186.     ///
187.     /// Reads the entry at `index`.
188.     ///
189.     /// Returns `None` if the raw value is invalid according to `E::from_raw()`.
190.     ///
191.     /// # Safety
192.     ///
193.     /// The memory at `base + index * size_of::<PteWord>()` must be valid for a volatile read.
194.     ///
195.     // Trust boundary (see `verus-ai-logs/.../tcb-allowed.md` and `verus-unsupported.md`):
196.     // materializes a raw `*const PteWord` from the integer base address (`usize as *const`) and
197.     // performs a volatile load — the hardware page-table access. Verus does not support the
198.     // `usize -> *const T` cast, so the body cannot be verified; this mirrors the
199.     // `bump_allocator::alloc` / `frame::instance` int-to-pointer materialization boundaries.
200.     // The `ensures` pins the (trusted) result to the global page-table memory ghost, exactly as
201.     // `frame::instance` pins its result to `phys_view()` — no exec signature change.
202.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
203.     #[verus_spec(result =>
204.         requires
205.             index@ < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
206.         ensures
207.             result == spec_table_read::<E>(self@.addr, index@),
208.     )]
209.     pub unsafe fn read(&self, index: TableIndex) -> Option<E> {
210.         let offset: usize = index.into_raw() << PTE_WORD_SIZE_LOG2;
211.         let ptr: *const PteWord = (self.base + offset) as *const PteWord;
212.         E::from_raw(::core::ptr::read_volatile(ptr))
213.     }
214. 
215.     ///
216.     /// # Description
217.     ///
218.     /// Writes `entry` at `index`.
219.     ///
220.     /// # Safety
221.     ///
222.     /// The memory at `base + index * size_of::<PteWord>()` must be valid for a volatile write.
223.     ///
224.     // Trust boundary (see `tcb-allowed.md` / `verus-unsupported.md`): materializes a raw
225.     // `*mut PteWord` from the integer base address and performs a volatile store — the hardware
226.     // page-table write. The `usize -> *mut T` cast is unsupported by Verus, so the body cannot be
227.     // verified; same int-to-pointer boundary as `read`.
228.     //
229.     // No contents `ensures`: page-table memory is *mutable* volatile state, but `write` takes
230.     // `&self` and the global ghost `spec_table_word(addr, index)` is a *pure* function (one fixed
231.     // value per slot). Pinning that pure cell to the caller-chosen `entry` in an `external_body`
232.     // (hence *assumed*) postcondition is unsound — two writes of distinct entries to the same slot
233.     // would assume `spec_entry_raw(e1) == spec_entry_raw(e2)`, and with `lemma_entry_roundtrip`
234.     // that derives `e1 == e2`, i.e. `false`. The slot-update transition
235.     // (`self@.entries[index@] == Some(entry)` after the call, with all other slots framed) is a
236.     // genuine `old@ -> @` state change and is therefore *deferred to the proving-phase page-table
237.     // permission token* — exactly the deferral convention used by `identity_map_view()`'s
238.     // `v -> v'` in `identity_map.spec.rs` (a global accessor whose cross-call transition is
239.     // realized later by a ghost token, "not a verification escape"). Only the sound `requires`
240.     // (in-range index, auto from `TableIndex::inv`) is kept here.
241.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
242.     #[verus_spec(
243.         requires
244.             index@ < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
245.     )]
246.     pub unsafe fn write(&self, index: TableIndex, entry: E) {
247.         let offset: usize = index.into_raw() << PTE_WORD_SIZE_LOG2;
248.         let ptr: *mut PteWord = (self.base + offset) as *mut PteWord;

# Proof Extraction

Extract large inline `proof { ... }` blocks from exec code into named lemmas
in the proof file (`<module>.proof.rs`).

## Why

Large inline proof blocks hurt readability and make exec code hard to review.
Extracting them into lemmas with clear names documents *what* is being proven
and makes proofs reusable.

## Tool

Use `check_proof_blocks` (MCP tool) or the CLI script to find blocks:

```bash
python3 scripts/check_proof_blocks.py <source_file> --threshold 5 --all
```

Output shows each proof block with its enclosing function, line range, and size.
Blocks marked `⚠️ EXTRACT` exceed the threshold.

## Rules

| Block size  | Action |
|-------------|--------|
| >5 lines    | **Must** extract into a lemma in `.proof.rs` |
| 4-5 lines   | Extract if generic/reusable; keep if tightly coupled to exec context |
| 1-3 lines   | Keep inline |

## Extraction Process

For each block to extract:

1. Read the proof block and identify what it proves (the key `assert` / property).
2. Create `proof fn lemma_<descriptive_name>` in `.proof.rs` with:
   - `requires`: the preconditions the proof depends on
   - `ensures`: the property being proven (must be strong enough for the call site)
3. Replace the inline block with a 1-3 line lemma call.
4. Run verification to confirm it still passes.

## Naming

Lemma names describe what they prove:
- ✅ `lemma_set_bit_preserves_inv`
- ✅ `lemma_alloc_range_bounded`
- ❌ `lemma_proof_block_1`
- ❌ `lemma_helper`

## Constraints

- Do NOT change exec logic.
- Do NOT change spec function signatures.
- Verification must still pass after extraction.

=== PROOF-MINIMIZATION ===
---
name: proof-minimization
description: "Remove redundant proof artifacts (assertions, lemmas, hints, dead code) without weakening guarantees. Use when polishing verified code to reduce verbosity."
---

# Proof Minimization

Remove redundant proof artifacts to make verification lean and readable
without weakening any guarantees.

## What to Remove

1. **Redundant lemmas** — another lemma proves the exact same property
   (same `requires` AND same `ensures`).
2. **Redundant assertions** — `assert` statements that Verus can verify
   without them. Remove in bulk, then re-run verification.
3. **Redundant proof hints** — unnecessary `by`, `by(nonlinear_arith)`,
   or trigger annotations that Verus doesn't need.
4. **Dead spec functions** — non-public spec functions with zero callers (not
   referenced in any `requires`, `ensures`, `invariant`, or lemma). Keep
   `pub` spec functions — they may be part of the module's API for dependents.
5. **Debug artifacts** — In spec/proof files: remove TODO comments, commented-out
   code, and property-ID annotations (e.g., `// FUNC-POST-3`, `// INV-2`). In
   exec files: remove unnecessary verification-related comments (e.g., obsolete
   proof hints, property-ID tags); do NOT remove original source comments.

## What is NOT Redundant

- **Uncalled lemmas**: Verus verifies all lemmas regardless of callers.
  An uncalled lemma still proves a property. Only remove if another lemma
  proves the *exact* same thing.
- **Different preconditions**: Two lemmas with different `requires` prove
  different properties even if `ensures` looks similar.

**When in doubt, keep it.**

## Process

This is a best-effort pass for readability, not an exhaustive search.

1. **Assertions**: Remove `assert` statements that look redundant based on context.
2. **Lemmas**: Remove a lemma only if another has identical `requires` + `ensures`.
3. **Proof hints**: Remove `by(...)` annotations that look unnecessary.
4. Re-run verification after changes — if it fails, revert the removal.

## Constraints

- Do NOT add `assume`, `admit`, or `external_body`.
- Do NOT weaken any `ensures` or remove any meaningful property.
- Verification must pass after every removal batch.

name: verus-constraints
description: "Mandatory rules for writing Verus code. Covers verus! block syntax, source integrity for exec code, forbidden patterns, and assume_specification policy. Must be followed whenever producing or modifying Verus-annotated code."
---

# Verus Constraints

Study `docs/examples/binary-search/proof/` for a complete example following all
constraints below.

## verus! { } Blocks Only

All spec and proof code **must** use native `verus! { }` block syntax.
Do **not** use attribute-based syntax (`#[verus_spec]`, `#[verus_verify]`, `proof! { }`).

```rust
// ✅ CORRECT
verus! {
    fn foo(x: u32) -> (ret: u32)
        requires x < 100,
        ensures ret == x + 1,
    { x + 1 }
} // verus!

// ❌ WRONG — attribute style
#[verus_spec(ret => requires x < 100, ensures ret == x + 1)]
fn foo(x: u32) -> u32 { x + 1 }
```

Even if existing code uses attribute style, write all new code in `verus! { }` style.
Attribute style is less mature; `verus! { }` can be auto-converted later.

## Source Integrity (exec code)

The following rules apply to the original source files (e.g. `lib.rs`), not to
`*.spec.rs` / `*.proof.rs` which are freely editable.

Verus verification is **in-place**: specs and proofs are added directly alongside
exec code. The annotated code remains fully compilable and runnable — Verus
constructs are erased during normal `cargo build` via cfg-gating. Do not change
code logic; keep changes minimal so developers can review diffs easily.

**Preserve:** exec logic, function signatures, struct definitions, comments,
debug assertions, and all other existing code. If a construct is unsupported by
Verus (e.g. `debug_assert!`), cfg-gate it with `#[cfg(not(verus_keep_ghost))]`
rather than deleting.

**Allowed additions:** `verus! { }` blocks (requires, ensures, invariants, decreases,
proof blocks, assert), vstd imports (cfg-gated), named returns `-> (ret: T)`,
ghost/tracked variables, `#[cfg_attr(not(verus_keep_ghost), derive(...))]` gating.

**Never change:** semantic code logic or function/struct signatures. Exception:
only if Verus genuinely cannot express a construct — first search vstd for
alternatives, build a minimal reproducer proving unsupported, then make the
smallest change needed and document why.

**Iterator rewrite rule:** When exec code uses Iterator chains
(`.iter().filter().map().collect()`), these MUST be rewritten to while
loops because Iterator API is unsupported. This is a permitted exec
change because: (1) the behavioral semantics are identical, (2) it is
a true Verus limitation, (3) the ensures should describe the ORIGINAL
functional intent using `Seq::filter`/`Seq::map_values`, not the
rewritten loop structure.

**After completing all changes**, use the `ast-consistency` skill to verify
source integrity. Fix all inconsistencies. For unavoidable ones, you must
confirm: (1) the code still builds with `cargo build`, (2) semantic code logic
is unchanged, (3) it is a genuine Verus limitation, and (4) it is documented.

## Forbidden Patterns
